slide1.headline: Cerebras Makes a Splash in Nasdaq Debut
slide1.subtitle: AI chipmaker's market cap soars to $95 billion

slide2.title: WHAT HAPPENED
lines: Cerebras Systems, an AI chipmaker, debuted on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on May 14, 2026.
The company's stock price surged 68% on its first day of trading.
This increase pushed Cerebras' market capitalization to $95 billion.
The company's initial public offering (IPO) was valued at $5.6 billion.

slide3.title: WHY IT MATTERS
lines: Cerebras' successful IPO is a significant indication of the growing interest in AI technology.
The company's wafer-scale AI processors are designed to increase computing power and reduce energy consumption.
This innovation has the potential to revolutionize various industries, including healthcare, finance, and transportation.

slide4.title: INSIGHTS
bullets: The AI chip market is expected to experience rapid growth in the coming years.
Cerebras' technology has the potential to disrupt traditional computing architectures.
The company's success may attract more investments in the AI sector.

slide1.headline: EU AI Act Delay: What Does it Mean?
slide1.subtitle: A temporary reprieve for AI developers

slide2.title: WHAT HAPPENED
lines: The EU AI Act has been delayed, giving AI developers a temporary reprieve.
The delay provides an opportunity for developers to prepare for the new regulations.
The EU AI Act aims to establish a regulatory framework for the development and deployment of AI systems.
The act is expected to have a significant impact on the AI industry, with potential fines of up to $25 million for non-compliance.

slide3.title: INSIGHTS
bullets: The delay may allow AI developers to better understand the regulations and prepare for compliance.
The EU AI Act may set a precedent for other regions to establish similar regulations.
The act's impact on the AI industry will depend on the final implementation and enforcement.
